meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I've spent four of them in the hallway reading a gradebook entry for Owen. Who decided on a zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
Okay. You asked for this meeting, Hale. Who decided on the zero?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a written promise that nothing goes on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a trip to the principal's office if she doesn't get them.
What moved her: Nothing, because the only thing Hale said was a pleasantry and it gave her no document or answer to weigh.
What cost ground: Answering her direct question about who decided on the zero with thanks for coming in, because it dodged the question and let her keep control of the meeting.
Try next time: Right after she asks who decided and whether anyone spoke to Owen, answer both plainly in one sentence, own that the zero went in before the call home, and then put a dated document in front of her.
